name: Fruit Pin Wheels
description: Historical recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book (1914). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: large spoonful of slightly melted butter
ingredients.originalText: a large spoonful of slightly melted butter

instructions.text: Mix sifted flour, sugar, salt, and baking powder
Rub in butter, and mix into a moderately stiff dough with half a pint of milk
Sprinkle the pastry board with flour, turn out the dough and roll it to a large square about half an inch thick
Spread a large spoonful of slightly melted butter on this
Add one cupful of Demerara sugar, and one cupful of well-cleaned currants
Grate a little nutmeg over the sugar and currants
Roll up just like a jelly roll or poly-poly
Cut the roll into slices about three-quarters of an inch thick
Place them upon a well-buttered baking shell or tin, but do not let the slices touch

source.author: Grace E. Denison
source.originalInstructions:
1. Mix sifted flour, sugar, salt, and baking powder
2. Rub in butter, and mix into a moderately stiff dough with half a pint of milk
3. Sprinkle the pastry board with flour, turn out the dough and roll it to a large square about half an inch thick
4. Spread a large spoonful of slightly melted butter on this
5. Add one cupful of Demerara sugar, and one cupful of well-cleaned currants
6. Grate a little nutmeg over the sugar and currants
7. Roll up just like a jelly roll or poly-poly
8. Cut the roll into slices about three-quarters of an inch thick
9. Place them upon a well-buttered baking shell or tin, but do not let the slices touch
